data.name: Try Hard Parking
data.detailed_description:
Nova atualização

The game will get 2 New Level Updates every month or so, all your existing Steam Achievements and best times will stay, so no worries. Also the latest Update has volume control for music(Page Up/Down) and main sound (Mouse scroll up/down) along with better vehicle controls and Damage effects.


Acerca do jogo

Welcome to "The Hardest and most rage inducing Parking Game in The World", just give it a try.

Tempt fate & physics as you navigate obstacle courses in pursuit of your holy parking spot in this 80s retro environment in Try Hard Parking! . Put your driving skills to the test in this retro styled game as you jump,drop and carefully steer across levels full of obstacle to reach your holy parking lot. This is not your typical parking game. We have so many driving games these days that they are proud of their driving skills. Do a good time and throw the controller to a friend and see all his driving skills diminish.

Feature List :

  • 10 Unique Crazy Levels with Different Vehicles ranging from 80s known Cars to A-Team's Van.
  • Difficult, Fun, Fast, Frustrating and Rage Inducing Gameplay with great music to keep your cool.
  • Game Trophies such as "Grand ma" for slowest and "Takumi 86" for Fastest or "Super Tuber" for extreme players.

  • Some Trophies can only be achieved within a limited amount of tries after that its gone (Consequence filled Score Resetting, which makes you lose all your best times)
  • Steam Achievements with some levels with hidden achievement. (Do "Trial 1" in under 45 seconds and 5 Tries, to get a cool achievement)

Don't lose your Zen, it only gets harder -> "be in the zone".

  • Hit "ENTER" or "Start" on Xbox360 Controller to Quickly Reset if your vehicle is stuck(which will be a lot of times). It resets the timer too, but keeps the number of tries.
  • Use pulses of Acceleration: Don't Go full throttle , use short bursts of speed.
  • Use Handbrake turns: Use brakes and handbrakes, rear wheel slides to get the car in to position.
  • Keep wheels in contact : Try to be keep your wheels in contact for traction.
  • Don't get stuck : The car gets stuck easily on corners & ledges, so it requires a bit of precision to drive.

Note :

I really believe in "Try Before you Buy model", therefore suggest you type "Try Hard Parking" in YouTube and see some Gameplays before you buy the game, so that you are sure what you are getting. The steam GreenLight page has a demo for you to play. Thank you. Also please don't give thumb down, because you
find it hard.

The style and camera view of Try Hard Parking pays homage to Neo DriftOut & OverTop for NeoGeo 1994.

Soundtrack Artists:

  • Evan King
  • Jeremy Lelis

Navigation on Level Screen

- Click on the arrows on the level selection screen to move around different Level Grids.
- Mouse over Blocks too see Trophies (some are achievements).

Hi my name is Sayem Chaklader. I am a lonewolf developer who loves contributing to OpenSource Software.
Currently my 11 year nephew is my playtester (in exchange for Lays & Pringles).

data.short_description: "Hardest and most Rage Inducing Parking Game in The World". Navigate crazy obstacle courses in pursuit of your holy parking spot in this 80s Arcade Style driving game.

reviews.review:
Developed and published by gearspecs, Try Hard Parking takes an everyday driving activity and turns it into an unapologetically difficult arcade challenge. At first glance, its premise sounds simple: park your car at the designated spot. However, the game quickly reveals itself to be anything but ordinary. Rather than focusing on realism, it leans heavily into over-the-top level design, demanding players navigate dangerous ramps, precarious platforms, and obstacle-filled environments where even the slightest mistake can result in failure. It is a game that wears its punishing nature proudly and makes no attempt to appeal to players looking for a laid-back driving experience.

The title embraces an old-school arcade philosophy where mastery comes only through repetition. Across its collection of handcrafted levels, players are tasked with controlling a variety of vehicles while balancing acceleration, braking, and momentum with precision. The top-down perspective offers a clear view of each challenge, but visibility alone does not make success any easier. Every course is designed to test patience, whether it involves landing jumps correctly, avoiding environmental hazards, or maintaining enough traction to stay on a narrow path. The game encourages experimentation and perseverance, often requiring dozens of attempts before a single successful run.

Visually, Try Hard Parking benefits from a charming retro aesthetic inspired by the vibrant style of the 1980s. Its selection of vehicles carries a distinct personality, with several paying homage to iconic automotive designs from pop culture. While the graphics are relatively simple, they suit the game's identity well and are complemented by a fitting soundtrack that keeps the energy high even during moments of frustration. The presentation never aims for technical excellence; instead, it focuses on creating a memorable atmosphere that reinforces its arcade roots.

Another noteworthy aspect is the game's reward structure. Players are not merely graded on completion but are also encouraged to improve their times and reduce the number of failed attempts. Unlockable trophies and hidden achievements add replay value, turning each level into a challenge to be perfected rather than simply finished. This emphasis on self-improvement gives the game a surprising amount of longevity despite its modest amount of content. Dedicated players will likely spend more time chasing ideal performances than completing the initial set of stages.

That said, the game's biggest obstacle is accessibility. Its steep difficulty curve can feel overwhelming, particularly for newcomers expecting a traditional parking simulator. The controls, while intentionally designed around precision, may initially feel unforgiving, and some players may struggle with the trial-and-error approach that defines the experience. The limited number of levels also means that enjoyment largely depends on how much satisfaction a player gets from overcoming difficult challenges. Those who thrive on persistence will appreciate what the game offers, while others may find its design philosophy unnecessarily punishing.

Ultimately, Try Hard Parking succeeds because it remains committed to its vision from beginning to end. It transforms a mundane concept into a skill-based arcade experience filled with humor, frustration, and moments of genuine accomplishment. While its niche appeal and uncompromising difficulty prevent it from becoming a universally recommended title, it stands as an entertaining example of how creativity and confidence can elevate a simple idea into something memorable.

Rating: 6/10

  • Processador: Single Core 2.0 Ghz
